quotes.speaker: D'Angelo Russell
quotes.summary_phrase: D'Angelo Russell on adapting to the CBA's high-level basketball IQ
quotes.excerpt: A lot of things you think is a regular read, to them it's like mechanic.
quotes.quote: Coach is afraid that because your basketball IQ is high level, maybe they get disconnected from your level. A lot of things you think is a regular read, to them it's like mechanic.

quotes.speaker: D'Angelo Russell
quotes.summary_phrase: D'Angelo Russell on implementing his own offensive system in the CBA
quotes.excerpt: If we say it's a color, that means stack.
quotes.quote: When I was on the Lakers I was like, everybody in the league is running stack. If we say it's a color, that means stack. Because everybody says Spain, Spain, and then the defense is like Spain, Spain, and they know it's stack. I hate AD and LeBron, if I say red, green, blue, that's stack. We could be on the free throw line, and start being like, blue, blue, and AD is like, no, no, no, indigo. And now it's like, they all confused, but y'all know it's the same shit because it's one color.

quotes.speaker: D'Angelo Russell
quotes.summary_phrase: D'Angelo Russell on drawing inspiration from Stephon Marbury's CBA legacy
quotes.excerpt: What Stephon Marbury did was something that I really want to try to inspire to be.
quotes.quote: A lot of guys have been here. You name the Tracy McGradys, the Amar'e Stoudemires, the Michael Beasleys, the Jared Sullingers, the Sullas. There's so many guys that have come over here and got to just hoop. For me, I think what Stephon Marbury did was something that I really want to try to inspire to be, and if not even better. You know, when you treat people right on the way, and I think that will leave my legacy behind in a way that I could never even imagine.
